mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, it predicts a near-term monetary tightening, which reduces discount rates and increases expected equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS MA(3) crosses above 4% in a non-tightening regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) above 200,000 suggests labor market acceleration, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, yielding positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite PAYEMS > 200,000 for ≥3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in monthly HOUST (residential construction) by more than 10% indicates weakening housing demand, which can depress economic momentum and produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during confirmed housing contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of 2% or more signals supply-side softness, reducing growth expectations and generating negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat when INDPRO declines by ≥2% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) rises by more than 0.2 percentage points over the next 3 months, it reflects labor market weakness that can depress equity valuations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly increases by >0.2pp over 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during UNRATE upswings >0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's levels indicate accelerating demand, which tends to boost earnings expectations and drive positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month AND RSAFS > previous month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when both proxies show simultaneous acceleration in a weak macro environment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly PAYEMS below 140,000 for two consecutive months suggests labor market softening, which can erode consumer spending and produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such labor softening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that can trigger rate hikes and dampen equity valuations, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly > previous month + 0.5% for 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such inflationary trends when central bank rates remain unchanged.
